subject: general
question: Zakir travels from City A to City B. If Zakir drives his car at (3)/(8) th of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 10 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Zakir would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed reduced to 3/8 ⇒ time increases by 8/3 times

Extra time = (8/3 − 1) = 5/3 of original time

(5/3) × T = 10 ⇒ T = 10 × (3/5) = 6

**∴ Answer = 6 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Reduced speed = 3/8 of normal speed

Delay = 10 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time ∝ 1/Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let normal time = T

⇒ New time = T × (8/3)

⇒ Delay = New time − Normal time

⇒ T × (8/3) − T = 10

⇒ T(8/3 − 1) = 10

⇒ T × (5/3) = 10

⇒ T = 10 × (3/5) = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relation

Time is inversely proportional to speed for fixed distance

Ratio Concept

If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a

Delay Formula

Delay = New time − Original time

Shortcut Insight

Extra time fraction directly helps find original time
